explanations: There is no defect. Keys are read from mounted files rather than hard-coded, and load errors report only the secret's name and an errno code, never its contents. Signatures are compared with timingSafeEqual after a length check, so timing does not leak the expected MAC. Log lines on rejection contain only a reason, the timestamp, and the body length, never the key, the computed signature, or the provided signature. The previous key is accepted only for verification, which is the standard way to rotate without downtime.

verify builds candidates from keys.current and keys.previous (filtering out null) and accepts if any matches. Old-key signatures still verify against keys.previous. The skew check is relative to now, not to rotation time, and no key-id header is read anywhere.

readSecretFile catches the read failure and throws SecretLoadError(name, code), producing 'secret courier_webhook_key unavailable: ENOENT'. The original error, including path, is not included in the message. No empty key is returned, and nothing was read.

The regex /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i requires exactly 64 hex characters, so a 32-character value is rejected with reason missing_or_malformed_headers before any signing. The length check in matches would also prevent a timingSafeEqual throw, but it is never reached here, and prefix matches are never accepted.
